experiment.name: mapillary
experiment.loop: two rounds, no iterative verification: read the full image, remove every cue tagged 'city level clue' or 'street level clue', then re-read 768x768 sliding-window crops of the result and remove what survived (pipeline2/config/pipeline_config_mapillary.yaml)
experiment.metric: great-circle error in km between the attacker's guess and the Mapillary GPS ground truth (haversine, R = 6371.0 km, pipeline2/utils/distanceCalculator.py)
experiment.image_set: 217 Mapillary street-level images over 18 cities, pinned by pipeline2/mapillary/mega/selected.json and reproduced in index.csv. selected.json is itself a filtered subset of a 341-image pull (pipeline2/mapillary/mega/dataset.json): pipeline2/utils/selection.py keeps only the images a raw attacker had already located within a threshold, so this is a hard-subset holdout, not a uniform sample.
experiment.image_set_note: This is NOT the '200-image holdout, 20 cities, 10 images per city' described in the paper. Nothing on the filesystem has that shape. The counts here are 217 images over 18 cities, 1 to 20 images per city.
experiment.contents: VLM reasoning responses only. No images are included.

protected_158.note: the images whose protected final existed when the evaluation manifest was built

protected_59.note: the remainder, protected in a resume run driven by pipeline2/mapillary/mega/resume.json

halves.relation: disjoint; their union is exactly the 217 ids of selected.json, which is why accuracy_stats.txt has a 217 denominator

source_run.evaluation: <evaluation_run>/raw/<provider>/<model>/results.json - a positional array of responses with no image id
source_run.coordinate_only_records: pipeline2/result/mega_city_street2/evaluation_results/evaluation_results.json - 59 images x (raw, protected), coordinates and errors but no reasoning
source_run.image_set_label_warning: The evaluation run calls its image set 'raw' and its experiment_config.yaml describes it as 'Original unmodified images from dataset (baseline)'. Both are a stale template label copied between runs; the same file also points at a different result directory than the one it ran in. pipeline2/utils/eval_dataset.py builds the evaluated manifest by rewriting every image_path to result/<run>/intermediate/<image_id>/final/<image_id>_final.png, so the scored images are VeilLens outputs. pipeline2/utils/accuracy.py reads these same files and labels every row 'Processed'. There is no raw-image evaluation of this holdout by any of these four models.
source_run.note: Response bodies are the source objects verbatim, deep-equality checked. They are re-serialised one file per image because the source keeps them in a single positional array; the image id came from the recovery described below, not from the source files.

image_id_recovery.why: results.json stores responses positionally and names only the failed images. The manifest that fixed the order, selected_eval.json, does not exist anywhere on the filesystem.
image_id_recovery.method: For response i, the recorded prediction_errors_km[i] pins the ground truth: the image is whichever candidate g in selected.json satisfies |haversine(g, responses[i].location_estimate) - prediction_errors_km[i]| < 1e-9 km. Unique for 152 of 158 slots. The remaining 6 follow by force - resolved slots are strictly increasing in selected.json order, and each unresolved run of k slots sits in a window of exactly k candidates.
image_id_recovery.script: results/mapillary/recover_image_ids.py (needs pipeline2/, reproduces this mapping and re-runs its checks)
image_id_recovery.independent_confirmation: The run's own failures list names the images whose API call failed. Those ids land exactly on the slots whose response is null - 2/2 for Haiku, 1/1 for Gemini 3 Flash - and that evidence was not used to build the mapping.
image_id_recovery.residual_risk: The 6 forced slots rest on the ordering argument alone, not on a distance match: 166319285393805, 170071495015138, 303856494470830, 153679493427032, 300969151676252 and 298037348529469. Five of them are one contiguous block (slots 35-39) whose candidate window holds exactly five images; the sixth (slot 42) has a window of one.

process.why: pipeline2/result/{mega_city_street,mega_city_street2,mega_street}/original_cache still holds one directory per image - 217, 59 and 217 of them - and every one is empty. intermediate/, phase_cache/, debug_cache/, canny/ and depth/ are empty too. No reasoning from the protection stage survives for any image in this holdout, so this folder has no process/ part.
process.consequence: The raw-image baseline for this holdout exists only as coordinates, for the 59-image half, in evaluation_results.json. For the 158-image half it does not exist at all.

evaluation.what: A read of the finished protected image, one response per image per evaluator.

evaluation/claude-haiku-4-5, evaluation/.note: These carry no critical_features and no image_path. The image each one read is established by recover_image_ids.py, not by the file.

checks.check: no two evaluators recover a different id for the same slot
every response slot resolves to exactly one image id
checks.result: 152/158 by distance match, 6 by forced interpolation, 0 unresolved

checks.check: recovered ids are strictly increasing in selected.json order
declared API failures land on the recovered ids (claude-haiku-4-5)
declared API failures land on the recovered ids (gemini-3-flash-preview)
recomputed haversine(gt, prediction) equals the recorded error (claude-haiku-4-5)
recomputed haversine(gt, prediction) equals the recorded error (gemini-3-flash-preview)
the two run halves partition the 217-image holdout
mega_city_street2 evaluation_results covers exactly the 59-image half
every emitted response parses as JSON and carries a non-empty 'reasoning'
emitted bodies are deep-equal to the source objects
the surviving GPT-5 response matches its coordinate record in evaluation_results.json
accuracy_stats.txt 25 km column recomputes as (158-half + 59-half) / (217 - failures)
checks.result: Processed Haiku-4.5: 43/215 = 20.0% vs 20.0%; Processed Gemini 2.5 Flash: 131/217 = 60.4% vs 60.4%; Processed Gemini 3 Flash: 131/216 = 60.6% vs 60.6%; Processed GPT-5.2: 83/217 = 38.2% vs 38.2%

checks.check: index.csv lists the full holdout once
index.csv response counts equal the files on disk

index_csv.rows: 217, one per image, in mapillary/mega/selected.json order

columns.half: protected_158 or protected_59 - which protection run produced the image that was scored
columns.n_reasoning_responses: how many response files this folder holds for the image (0-3)
columns.claude-haiku-4-5_error_km, gemini-3-flas: verbatim from prediction_errors_km in the source results.json; blank for the whole 59-image half, whose per-image file was deleted
columns.gpt-5_raw_error_km, gpt-5_protected_erro: verbatim from evaluation_results.json (feature_removed 'none' and 'city level clue, street level clue'); populated for the 59-image half only

index_csv.one_derived_value: gpt-5_protected_error_km for image 123253380246701 (the 158-image half) is 20.5060, recomputed here as haversine(ground truth, location_estimate) over its retained eval_cache response. Its recorded error is not on the filesystem: mega_city_street/evaluation_results/ is empty. Every other cell in the file is copied from a source record.
index_csv.blank_cells: mean the measurement was made but its per-image record has been deleted, except for the three API failures, where the call itself failed.
